notes: DISSENT DISCHARGED. My bright-disc dissent, recorded against draft-v8, is resolved by this amendment: both clauses I ruled unsatisfiable are gone, replaced by framing-independent property tests that the already-captured stills satisfy. Nothing in my lane is now outstanding as dissent, and my disposition rests only on the open runtime defects below. The craft ruling behind it stands on the record: the moon was never the defect. Exclusion-by-framing would have cost the spine its golden-section placement and the seam its +/-5 deg centering to satisfy bookkeeping, and the disc earns its place in both frames — a cold light beside the one kept fire, which is K11 made literal.

AMENDMENT RECORD (v8), my lane: two analytic derivations replacing two observed bands, plus a convention declaration. The root cause of three failed measurements was structural - spineQuaternion (spaceStationBody.ts:237) seeds the spine's azimuth and elevation, so projected extent is L·sin psi and no fixed percentage can hold across seeds. Because the ch10 leg flies the station centre in a straight line (autopilot.ts:323-328), psi is constant for the whole leg, and occupancy collapses to f = K/Z - varying with range alone. The formula predicts all eight strip frames at 0.973-0.980 of measured, a constant mask edge bias rather than drift. The tangent-correct declaration matters because linear and tangent conversions disagree at the boundary (7.911 vs 8.249 deg on the same frame); both of my angle terms now use one convention. The lens qualifier required no re-wording of my five no-authored-lens-motion statements: FOV = 70 + 9x boost is player-held input, so they were always true.

D-A1 COMPOSITION SUSPENSION LIFTED. renderCamera fov is identical to flightFeedback fov to 0.0000 deg across 24 frames, shell scale exactly reciprocal, aperture 613-789px (median 730) on the regenerated strips, and the 300px readings never reproduced. My draft-v7 standing condition suspending the verification-report composition verdicts is DISCHARGED, and measurements taken from the regenerated strips are admissible. The FOV-79 reading that briefly looked like a second lens is also resolved and was never a lens move: the autopilot rail asserted sprint = forward during ch10-transit, so the pilot flew with boost held; with that suppressed, transit holds 70.0-70.0, boost 0, shell scale 1.00000, zero frames above 73.72, and the leg still completes.

PROBE DEFECT STILL OPEN, routed to Integration, not blocking: the cut-line capture's hull and light instance counts are inverted because the corrective swap at ch10-v7-final-probe.mjs:262 is guarded on !hull.instanceColor, which never fires - both meshes call setColorAt. stationSpineGeom at the cut line is therefore measured over the 613 emissive instances rather than the 126 hull boxes. The differential mask channel is unaffected and is the instrument my occupancy law is written against, so the contract is sound; the geom channel simply cannot be cited for the cut line until the guard is fixed.

EVIDENCE GAP THAT BLOCKS EVALUATION OF MY OWN TERM: no spine axis, spine quaternion, or aspect angle psi is recorded anywhere in the run directory - the recorded offAxisDeg is the camera-to-centre angle, not a spine aspect. Until the probe logs psi at each shutter, the occupancy and seam laws cannot be evaluated by the verifier at all. This must land with the D-A2 and D-A4 re-shoots.

D-A1 RESOLUTION — ACCEPTED AS DIAGNOSIS, WITH THE EVIDENCE OBLIGATION IT CREATED LEFT OPEN. I accept the integration engineer's finding and withdraw D-A1 as a lens defect. The instrumentation is dispositive in a way my predecessor's pixel measurement could not be: all four profiles were instrumented and found bit-identical — one camera, matching FOVs, canopy approximately 690px everywhere — and the 300px frames exist only in strips captured at 01:20Z, before the D-10/D-13 autopilot fixes; replaying the same plans now yields full-size canopies. That is a coherent causal account (the pre-fix autopilot put the ship somewhere the post-fix autopilot does not, and the rig held screen anchors correctly the whole time), and it is confirmed by the mechanism my predecessor himself specified as the decisive probe: log the render camera per strip frame per profile. D-A1 is therefore reclassified critical-lens-defect -> stale-evidence. BUT acceptance of the diagnosis is not acceptance of the evidence: my predecessor's own escalation stands — 'until the LOW and HIGH families share one lens, every composition verdict in verification-report.json is unfounded' — and the fix to an unfounded verdict is a re-measurement, not a reclassification. The strips must be regenerated post-fix and EVERY composition verdict measured from them re-taken, specifically including the 31.8% spine reading that motivated ruling [e]'s 28-34% band. I sign the band because it is the honest expression of the shot's own intent at the shutter range, not because the 31.8% measurement survived; if the regenerated strips disagree with 28-34%, that is a contract question routed back to me, not an integrator judgement call.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE V6 ROUTED DEFECT: the same instrumentation bears on my draft-v6 STANDING condition (MEDIUM+reduced-motion reporting appliedFovDeg 75 where the other three tiers report 70). 'All four profiles bit-identical with matching FOVs' would discharge it, but the v6 defect was found by reading appliedFovDeg while D-A1 was found by measuring pixels, and I will not let one result close the other by implication. The condition stays STANDING until the post-fix four-variant state trace shows transit appliedFovDeg 70 on MEDIUM+reduced-motion explicitly.

AMENDMENT RECORD (v7), my lane: six rulings on the independent audit, all landed verbatim. [a] The audit was right that still-seam-of-light is not the seam — it was shot at range 955 with the station already resolved, so the three-distance thesis (dot -> line -> place) had no line. The new criterion makes the seam a LATCH-time capture with a falsifiable line test (7.5-8.2 degrees long, at most 2.4 degrees thick, no resolvable hull mass) plus a paired LOW frame, so the middle distance can never again be proved by a resolve frame. [b] The ST-0 still violated its own spec (camera at the Kestrel, no hearth in frame) and lost its subject to a large warm disc; the staging deltas re-tie the camera to the hearth (at most 25 units from the habitat-core handle, emissive in the bottom 20%) and the luminance claim is now a frame test — peak luminance is the frame maximum above the horizon band — rather than an unmeasurable 'above the brightest star'. Widening moon exclusion from 10 to 15 degrees of yaw is what buys that test its headroom. [c] galaxyInFrame:false was a name test that a purple nebula walked straight through; the replacement is perceptual and pixel-measured, and the berth ring — dock-offer geometry standing under a run whose whole claim is that no door is offered — is now suppressed under the docking predicate rather than merely un-centered. [d] and [f] convert two of my assertions into probes. [e] repairs my own prose in the direction the audit indicated. In three of the six the audit found my sentence wrong and my staging right; in [b] and [c] it found the frame wrong. Both verdicts are accepted.

WHAT THE [c] EDIT DID NOT LOSE, checked because a name-test removal can quietly take a real exclusion with it: v6's cut-line criterion ended 'no galaxy, planet or home fire in frame', and v7 replaces that whole clause with the perceptual term. The exclusion itself survives undamaged at two other sites — shots[11]/focalHierarchy/negativeSpaceIntent still reads 'no galaxy, no planet, no home fires in frame — both fires are explicitly behind the camera, which is K11's geometry made literal', and the GALAXY FIREWALL at evidence/acceptanceCriteria/9 still binds both transit HIGH stills. The capture criterion now tests dominance and the shot still tests absence; nothing was traded away.

DOC-DRIFT OBSERVATION, non-blocking, routed to the next cycle rather than patched here (patching it would be authorship): four sites still carry the mobile figure 'about 26% of frame width' — story/agencyWindows/6/mobileBehavior, variants/mobile/preservedFocalSubject, shots/11/framing/mobileSafeArea, shots/11/lens/mobileCropRisk. That 26% was derived as the 844x390 counterpart of the old desktop 31%. Ruling [e] replaced the desktop figure with a 28-34% band, and shots[11]'s occupancy intent now says only 'narrower at 844x390' with no number. Scaling the old pair's ratio onto the new band gives roughly 23.5-28.5%, so 26% falls inside it and no site is contradicted, no staging changes, and the mobile terms remain satisfiable as written. But 26% is now a number that has outlived its derivation — exactly the D-A7 failure class — and if the verifier is asked to measure mobile occupancy against a band it must be re-derived by me first.

CHAPTER AND SCORE ITEMS IN THIS AMENDMENT, reviewed for collision with my lane and found clean: the new station-transit-reboard rung (no capture collision, no new chip width, marker clears at ignite well before any composed still); the T1 ignite rung's restriction to aboard-only publication (which removes a [SPACE] instruction shown to a player on foot — an honesty repair my lane supports, since the frame may not promise what the runtime does not do); the deferral standing line (a HUD-copy term, no focal consequence, and it prevents a mandatory objective from being invisible); the declined exit rung (Chapter's call, correctly reasoned from ch8 precedent, no image consequence); the mobile work-order exception (recorded as the shipped whole-game baseline and routed as a whole-game packet — I accept that it is not a ch10 defect, and note that on touch the K1 caption carries arrival independently, which is a composition fact in my favour); and Score's three humanize wording fixes (uniform velocity, zero drop probability, fixed articulation), which restate the same machine-time law in implementable terms and touch nothing of mine.
